diagnosis.root_cause: The customer's own fibre path is marginal and oscillating between degraded and critical RX levels, causing repeated link/session interruptions. The telemetry starts already in the degraded band, so this is signal-driven flapping rather than a newly declining fibre link. TX power, TX bias, distance, OLT, router, VLAN, and RADIUS state are healthy.
evidence: The subscriber is currently online and responds definitively, while all probed peers on EPON0/2 are also online; there is no ONU, splitter, or PON-port outage.
Peers have normal RX power while this ONU is around -27 to -28 dBm, isolating the problem to the customer's own optical path.
RX telemetry repeatedly swings between approximately -24 and -28.6 dBm, including critical readings, while TX power remains near the healthy 2.3 dBm mean.
TX bias remains stable around 11 mA and distance remains constant at 302 m, ruling out laser ageing and distance/path-record change.
The seven-day series begins in the degraded RX band and therefore does not meet the defined declining-link criterion; it represents a marginal link oscillating in and out of usable range.
The customer has 16 sessions in 24 hours with short approximately 71-minute average duration, exceeding the flapping threshold of 8 sessions and confirming signal-driven session flapping.
OLT reachability, SNMP, CPU, memory, temperature, router heartbeat, VLAN 1092, and RADIUS/CRM consistency are all normal, so infrastructure and authentication faults are not supported.

remediation.action: Dispatch fibre maintenance for this subscriber path: inspect and clean connectors, check bends/splices and the drop fibre, and test the splitter/drop optical path. Replace or repair the affected fibre segment or connectors if loss is confirmed. Continue monitoring RX stability and session count after repair; no OLT, router, VLAN, or RADIUS changes are indicated.

ground_truth.root_cause: RX power oscillates between roughly -24.4 and -28.2 dBm on an eleven hour cycle, crossing the threshold at which the link stops being usable. The session drops follow the signal excursions.
expected_reasoning: Sixteen sessions in 24 hours against a 2-3 baseline, with a 71 minute mean duration
Cached RX is -26.28 dBm, already in the degraded band
Telemetry shows RX oscillating between about -24.4 and -28.2 dBm on an eleven hour cycle
The lower excursions cross -28 dBm, at which point the link becomes unusable
Live RX of -27.94 confirms the signal is currently near the bottom of that swing
TX power, bias current, supply voltage and distance are all stable, so the ONU is healthy
RADIUS is clean with a single consistent entry and no mismatches
Peers on EPON0/2 read normal, so the fault is in this customer's own path
The session pattern tracks the signal excursions, so the optical fault explains the flapping
distractors: The trigger names the session count, pointing at the auth layer
Sixteen disconnects is well within the observed flapping tail and could be read as a CPE fault
